extracted.intended_audience: nonprofit staff and communicators (development, marketing, executive directors) responsible for planning, writing, designing, and publishing annual reports
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning, writing, designing, and publishing short nonprofit annual reports that communicate accomplishments, thank supporters, explain finances, and drive action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-planning clarity: three guiding questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Before getting started, answer three questions: What are your accomplishments for the year? What do you want supporters to remember about this year? What format will the report take?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three questions set goals and scope for the report; use them to guide content selection, messaging, and format decisions before drafting or designing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning steps for a short annual report
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a structured planning process — the author recommends seven planning steps specifically for a short annual report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow a concise planning checklist (the page references 'seven planning steps') to keep the report focused and short; adapt steps to your organization's needs. (Specific steps are not enumerated on this page excerpt.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Define how you will measure the success of the report
rubrics_metrics.description: Think ahead about how you’ll measure the success of your report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide key performance indicators (e.g., donor retention, new donors, website visits, shares, direct responses) and how you'll collect metrics to evaluate impact after distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accomplishments over activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Feature accomplishments as opposed to activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame content around outcomes and impact (what changed, whom you helped) rather than listing events or internal activities; prioritize measurable results and clear benefits to stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include stories from real people you serve
rubrics_metrics.description: Use stories from real people you serve to illustrate impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Center human stories and testimonials to make accomplishments concrete and emotionally resonant; keep stories focused, permissioned, and connected to the report’s key messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain the financials in plain language
rubrics_metrics.description: Present your financials explained in plain language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid jargon and complex accounting tables; summarize revenues, expenses, and financial health in clear, accessible terms so supporters can understand how funds were used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give ample thanks to your supporters
rubrics_metrics.description: Include ample thanks to your supporters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prominently acknowledge donors, volunteers, partners, and staff; express gratitude in a way that reinforces relationships and encourages continued support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a clear call to action
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a call to action in the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tell readers exactly what you want them to do next (e.g., give, volunteer, sign up, share); make the CTA prominent and easy to follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Donor list is optional and often unnecessary
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual report donor list is considered by the author to be 'a stupid waste of time' — do not feel obligated to include it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you choose to include a donor list, ensure it has clear purpose and value to readers; otherwise prioritize space for impact stories and calls to action.

rubrics_metrics.name: If including donor names, avoid outdated honorifics (e.g., 'Mr. and Mrs.')
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are going to do a donor list, stop using Mr. and Mrs. in your annual report donor lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use inclusive, modern naming conventions that respect individual identities and avoid assuming household naming norms; the page emphasizes that continuing to use 'Mr. and Mrs.' is a terrible idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Director letter is optional
rubrics_metrics.description: You can probably drop the Letter from the Executive Director, but guidance is provided if you need to keep it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If retained, keep the letter short, purposeful, and aligned with the report’s main message rather than a generic yearly recap (the page promises specific advice for when a letter must be kept).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer short annual reports over long 'behemoths'
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend a short annual report compared to the 30–50 page behemoths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shorter reports (postcards, 1–4 pages, infographics) are more likely to be read and shared; focus on concise storytelling, essential metrics, and strong visuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider digital formats and alternative sizes (postcards, pocket-sized, 2–4 page, infographics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many nonprofits have ditched print entirely and gone digital; also consider formats like pocket-sized, postcards, two-page, four-page, or infographic annual reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose format based on audience and budget: postcards and one-pagers for quick updates; 2–4 page layouts for slightly more depth; infographics for visual summarization; digital delivery can save costs and increase reach. The page links to multiple real-world examples and case studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use templates / suggested layouts (e.g., 4-page layouts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use available annual report templates and suggested layouts (the site offers 'Suggested Layouts for a 4-Page Annual Report').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage tested templates to streamline design and ensure a logical flow (cover, impact highlights, story/financials, call to action/acknowledgments). Request or download template(s) to speed production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use examples and case studies to inspire design and content choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Look at many real examples (postcards, infographics, pocket-sized reports, video annual reports) to inform your approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review curated examples and YouTube video annual reports to see what works in practice and adapt ideas that match your audience and goals.
